claims.text: Depositing a nitrogen-doped DLC coating by PECVD over a graded adhesion interlayer will improve the surface properties of high-performance stainless steel or nickel-based superalloy components.
The coating system will increase surface hardness relative to an untreated surface.
The coating system will reduce friction relative to an untreated surface.
The coating system will improve wear resistance relative to an untreated surface.
The coating system will improve corrosion and pitting resistance relative to an untreated surface.
Untreated high-performance stainless steel or nickel-based superalloy surfaces are prone to wear, friction, and corrosion under extreme operating conditions.
The graded adhesion interlayer alleviates thermal-expansion mismatch between the substrate and the DLC coating.
The graded adhesion interlayer improves coating-to-substrate bond strength.
The deposited coating forms a nanoscale, dense amorphous-carbon matrix containing nanocrystalline diamond domains and controlled nitrogen content.
The graded interlayer creates a tailored transition in thermal-expansion properties from the substrate to the coating.
The graded interlayer minimizes residual stresses at the substrate-coating interface.
The nitrogen-doped DLC acts as a barrier that reduces friction and wear.
Nanocrystalline diamond domains promote crack deflection.
Nanocrystalline diamond domains increase resistance to pitting and chemical attack under cyclic thermal and mechanical stresses.
The coating system will sustain its performance at temperatures up to 500 °C.
The coating system will remain effective in chlorinated solutions or high-pressure oxidizing atmospheres.
The coating system will remain effective under cyclic mechanical loading.
A poorly engineered graded interlayer may produce residual stresses or delamination during extreme thermal cycling.
Prior studies support short-term improvements in mechanical and surface properties from DLC coatings and nitrogen doping.
